items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The script is short (41 lines, 1033 bytes) and copies the reference solve.sh the agent read at step [16], so it is easy to follow. But it has no docstrings, and the deny-list ['frame','iframe','object','embed'] sits inline instead of in a named constant.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: A single remove_js function behind a main guard is fine. But the policy is hardcoded inline with no named allow/deny constants, and URL handling is a chained str.replace('javascript:', '').replace('<script', ...) rather than a normalisation helper.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It checks the argument count and prints a usage message. But open(filename, 'r') and open(filename, 'w') have no explicit encoding and no error handling for missing or unreadable files.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: It relies on case-sensitive literal replacement: .replace("javascript:", "") and .replace("/// and are not handled by general rules. It passed only because it copied the solution the tests were built around.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Only the dangerous tags and on* attributes are removed, but the whole document is re-serialised with str(soup), which changes quoting and self-closing tags. The global replace of 'javascript:' also edits ordinary text content.
